Tired of heavy ORMs getting in the way of your database performance? Meet Reylo: import raw SQL files directly into TypeScript with zero code generation and full end-to-end type inference. 🚀

Building high-performance apps usually means choosing between writing raw SQL for maximum control or using an ORM to keep TypeScript happy. Reylo bridges that gap entirely. By querying your dev database during compilation, it automatically infers precise column types, parameter constraints, nullability, and return cardinality straight from your .sql files—without requiring clunky build steps or watch processes. 

✨ Key Features You Will Love:

• Zero Code Generation: Powered by TypeScript content mappers and the --runExternalCode flag for a seamless developer experience.
• Real-Time Type Checking: Catch syntax errors, misspelled columns, and parameter mismatches instantly in your editor and right inside tsc.
• Bring Your Own Driver: Works with a massive range of Postgres, MySQL, and SQLite drivers including pg, mysql2, better-sqlite3, and Bun.sql.
• Smart Runtime Inference: Automatically maps your queries to single rows, null-safe lookups, arrays, or void based on unique keys and operators.

Whether you are building complex analytical APIs or empowering AI coding agents to safely write and modify raw SQL alongside your TypeScript code with guaranteed type validation, Reylo keeps your stack lightning fast and strictly typed. 

👉 Check it out on GitHub and star the project to support the maintainer:
https://github.com/colinhacks/reylo

🔓 Say goodbye to device-side runtime dumping for iOS apps! 

Decrypt iOS applications entirely offline by independently deriving FairPlay page keys using custom Python-based SINF and SUPF record parsing. 📱💻

Tired of relying on active device-side runtime dumping tools to analyze protected iOS binaries? EthanArbuckle/fairplay-decrypt solves this exact bottleneck. By leveraging a single 16-byte account credential retrieved from a jailbroken device, this tool parses app-specific SINF and SUPF metadata records, derives the necessary cryptographic page keys, decrypts encrypted arm64 Mach-O slices, and automatically clears cryptographic protection flags. 

Whether you are automating security scanning pipelines for internal enterprise iOS builds or studying the inner workings of Apple DRM architecture, this pure Python implementation gives you total control without manual device interaction.

Key Features:
🐍 Pure Python implementation that executes seamlessly on both macOS and Linux environments
📊 Comprehensive support for version-3 and version-5 SUPF structures along with 448-byte and padding-compliant 440-byte SINF priv records
🛠️ Integrated credential retrieval companion system designed for jailbroken iOS devices using Xcode and ldid
⚡ Targeted extraction and page-level decryption of encrypted arm64 Mach-O binaries alongside automated cryptid clearing

Ideal for security researchers, reverse engineers, mobile application developers, and digital forensics specialists looking to deep-dive into Apple digital rights management and applied cryptography.

Check out the repository and level up your static analysis pipeline today:
https://github.com/EthanArbuckle/fairplay-decrypt

Ever tried extracting a massive AI model checkpoint, game asset bundle, or multi-gigabyte dataset on a laptop or CI/CD runner, only to be hit with an "Out of Disk Space" error right at the end? 🛑

Traditional archive tools like unzip or 7-Zip force you to have double the disk space: you need enough room for the compressed archive AND the full uncompressed output sitting side-by-side. 

Meet HatchZip: a Rust-powered CLI utility that extracts massive archives in-place by shrinking the archive file as its contents hatch. 🚀

By reading archives from the end and truncating finished segments on-the-fly, the disk space freed up by the archive is immediately reused for your extracted files. No more 2x disk space penalties!

✨ Key Features:
• True in-place shrinkage for ZIP, 7z, tar, gz, and RAR volume sets
• Pre-flight safety checks that calculate exact space requirements and maintain a safety margin before touching your files
• Crash-resilient processing that lets interrupted extractions safely pick up where they left off
• File-chunk hole-punching on supported filesystems (ext4, XFS, btrfs, tmpfs) to reclaim space even faster
• A modular core library (hatchzip-core) ready to integrate into your own custom Rust tooling or pipelines

Whether you are managing tight storage limits on cloud runners or working with heavy datasets locally, HatchZip eliminates deployment bottlenecks and build failures.

Check out the repo, star it if it saves your disk, and let us know what you think:
https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip

Turn Claude into a disciplined day-trading co-pilot that scans thousands of charts, simulates 10,000 outcomes, and executes paper trades only with your explicit approval. 📈🤖

Building quantitative trading workflows into modern AI assistants usually requires complex, expensive infrastructure and brittle APIs. 

Jakeschincariol/day-trader-skill bridges modern AI assistant tooling with quantitative day-trading workflows by providing a modular pack of eleven Claude skills backed by plain Python tools. It automates the end-to-end trading pipeline from multi-thousand stock chart scanning and breaking news analysis to entry timing, risk management, Monte Carlo backtesting via a Time Machine simulation, and broker execution. 🚀

Notable Features:
• Modular Unix-philosophy pipeline where each skill reads output JSON from the previous step, flowing from scanner to risk manager to broker. 🔗
• Monte Carlo Time Machine simulation that replays 10,000 sessions derived from recent intraday bars to calculate objective historical odds before risking capital. 🎲
• Built-in guardrails including strict paper-trading defaults, mandatory manual approval steps via Claude chat prompts, and programmatic limit checking. 🛡️
• Zero-dependency standard-library Python backend that parses free public data feeds like Yahoo Finance charts, Nasdaq symbols, and SEC EDGAR without requiring external paid API keys. 🌐

Whether you are an algorithmic trader, an AI engineer building LLM agent plugins, or a software developer interested in quantitative finance, this repository gives you a blueprint for building domain-specific agentic skills that enforce safety constraints and human-in-the-loop validation for high-risk operations. 💻

Check out the repository here:

Stop paying the enterprise tax for workstation-grade compute. 

If you are training local LLMs, running heavy diffusion pipelines, or optimizing FlashAttention on consumer hardware, you need to see this. 

The Zagitta/gpu-unlock repository provides a Linux kernel module that unlocks workstation-grade FP and BF16 instruction rates on consumer NVIDIA RTX 3000 series cards (GA102, GA103, GA104, GA106) without modifying drivers or your UEFI.

🔥 THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES
Consumer NVIDIA Ampere cards are artificially limited compared to their data center equivalents. This tool configures speed selectors and executes a functional level reset prior to official driver binding. By writing specific SS0 and SS1 values, it effectively doubles the instruction issuing speed of FP and BF16 FMA operations into FP32 operations, bridging the performance gap for budget-conscious AI engineers.

🚀 KEY FEATURES
- Pre-Driver Initialization: Loads via an initramfs Linux kernel module so you never have to manually patch binaries after an NVIDIA driver update.
- Massive ML Boosts: Achieve up to an 80 percent increase in BF16 GEMM throughput for accelerated local LLM prefill and image generation.
- Flexible Target Configuration: Use kernel command-line arguments to selectively unlock specific PCI addresses or every supported card on multi-GPU rigs.
- Suspend-to-RAM Support: Robust power-management automatically restores your hardware unlock state after waking from sleep.
- VFIO-PCI Friendly: Fully compatible with virtual machine passthrough setups.

Whether you are building out a multi-GPU RTX 3090 rig for local model training or squeezing every ounce of performance out of your self-hosted inference pipeline, this repository is a game-changer for local AI infrastructure.

Check out the code and instructions on GitHub:
https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
